record.paper_title: Open Problems in the Function Theory of the Bergman Space
record.context_brief: Carathéodory-type theorem for Bergman zero divisors
record.original_question: Is every analytic function f on D satisfying ||f phi||_L2 ≤ ||phi||_H2 for every phi in H2(D) the normal limit of finite zero divisors for the Bergman space?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 5.2. Every analytic function f on D with ||f phi||_L2 ≤ ||phi||_H2, phi ∈ H2(D), is the normal limit of finite zero divisors.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{D}$ denote the open unit disk in the complex plane. The Hardy space $H^2(\mathbb{D})$ consists of analytic functions $\varphi(z)=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} a_n z^n$ on $\mathbb{D}$ with $\|\varphi\|_{H^2}^2 := \sum_{n=0}^\infty |a_n|^2 < \infty$. The Bergman space $L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ consists of analytic functions $g$ on $\mathbb{D}$ with $\|g\|_{L^2}^2 := \int_{\mathbb{D}} |g(z)|^2\, dA(z) < \infty$, where $dA$ is normalized area measure on $\mathbb{D}$.

For a finite set of points $\{z_1,\dots,z_n\}\subset \mathbb{D}$ (counted with multiplicities), the associated finite Bergman zero divisor is the unique extremal function $G \in L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ of unit norm that vanishes exactly on this set and maximizes $\operatorname{Re} G^{(k)}(0)$ at the lowest-order nonvanishing derivative; equivalently, it is the canonical contractive divisor associated with that zero set. Call an analytic function on $\mathbb{D}$ a "normal limit of finite zero divisors" if it is the limit, uniformly on compact subsets of $\mathbb{D}$, of a sequence of such finite Bergman zero divisors.

Question: Is it true that every analytic function $f$ on $\mathbb{D}$ satisfying
$$\|f\varphi\|_{L^2} \le \|\varphi\|_{H^2} \quad \text{for every } \varphi \in H^2(\mathbb{D})$$
is a normal limit of finite Bergman zero divisors?
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not find a published resolution of this specific conjecture concerning the characterization of normal limits of finite Bergman zero divisors via a contractive multiplier condition from $H^2$ into the Bergman space. Related work on contractive divisors and extremal functions in Bergman spaces by Hedenmalm, Duren, Khavinson, Shapiro, and Sundberg exists, but no source clearly settles this exact statement, so the status appears unknown.

status_evidence.title: Recent Progress in the Function Theory of the Bergman Space
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of progress and open problems on Bergman space zero divisors and contractive divisors.
status_evidence.claim: Survey indicates contractive-divisor problems remain active without a definitive resolution of this particular conjecture.

status_evidence.title: Contractive Zero-Divisors in Bergman Spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses contractive divisors G in A^p with ||f/G||_p ≤ ||f||_p for f vanishing on prescribed sets.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes background on contractive divisors but does not resolve the conjecture about normal limits.
